correctness.rationale: Arbitrary antiderivative tests in y and z give \(\mathbb E[x\mid y]=y\) and \(\mathbb E[x\mid z]=-(3/10)z\). Coordinate stationarity and \(L(y^2/2)=xy-y^2\) give \(\mathbb E[z]=\mathbb E[y^2]\) and \(\mathbb E[x]=\mathbb E[y]=-(3/10)\mathbb E[y^2]\), from which the sharp range and variance parabola follow. The two variance defects follow from the same moment identities, and their equality classes are exactly the two-equilibrium mixtures by invariant-support tangency. Stationarity of yz gives the exact \(7/13\) RMS-gap identity, whose equality support collapses to the origin. The packaged checker verifies all nonstandard polynomial algebra exactly.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies an exact stationary geometry tied to the two canonical equilibria: every compact stationary mean lies on their segment, while the complete y mean–variance pair lies on the Bernoulli interpolation parabola. This creates a nontrivial identifiability boundary—first two y moments alone cannot distinguish chaotic recurrence from an equilibrium mixture—and the two squared variance defects quantify precisely the missing dynamical information. The additional RMS ordering is exact and origin-rigid. These are natural invariant-measure diagnostics for a benchmark chaotic flow, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation of known Lyapunov data.
